extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, students, and researchers preparing notes and bibliographies in Chicago Notes & Bibliography style
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance for citing books and parts of books in the Chicago Manual of Style Notes and Bibliography system, including multivolume works, series, editions, places and publishers, dates, and special formats (microform, online supplements, self-published, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing multiple contributions to the same multiauthor book
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more contributions to the same multiauthor book are cited, the book itself, as well as the specific contributions, may be listed in the bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries for individual contributions may cross-refer to the book’s editor to avoid clutter. In notes, give full details the first time a work is mentioned, with subsequent references in shortened form (see also 14.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book-length work within a book (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the cited part of a book would normally be italicized if published alone, it may be italicized rather than placed in quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A play included in a collection may be italicized. See examples such as Thomas Bernhard, A Party for Boris, in Histrionics: Three Plays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing introductions, prefaces, afterwords
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is to a generic title (introduction, preface, afterword), that term (lowercased unless following a period) is added before the title of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the author of the introduction or other part is someone other than the main author, the author of the part comes first and the author of the book follows the title; in a bibliography entry include page number range for the part cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for letters in published collections
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to a letter (or memorandum or similar communication) in a published collection begins with the names of the sender and the recipient, in that order, followed by a date and sometimes the place where the communication was prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words such as letter, postcard, email are usually unnecessary; title of the collection is given in usual book form. If correspondents differ from those in the first full citation, a short form for the collection may be needed. For unpublished communications, see 14.214.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single letter in a bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is necessary to include a single letter in a bibliography, it is listed under the writer’s name only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Jackson, Paulina. Paulina Jackson to John Pepys Junior, October 3, 1676. In The Letters of Samuel Pepys and His Family Circle, edited by...

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing online-only supplements to books
rubrics_metrics.description: To cite an online-only supplement or enhancement to a book, include a title or a description for the content and a URL in addition to the publication details for the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify file format if applicable (e.g., PDF). Example given: include (PDF), online supplement to chap. 5 ... and URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editions other than the first (how to cite)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an edition other than the first is used or cited, the number or description of the edition follows the title in the listing and is abbreviated (e.g., 2nd ed.; rev. ed.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any information about volumes follows the edition number. Use wording as found on title/copyright pages and abbreviate consistently. See guidance for original date inclusion (14.114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint editions and modern editions (what to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication details—particularly the date—are relevant, include them; if page numbers are mentioned, specify the edition cited unless pagination is the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add information about different formats (paperback, electronic), additions of new material, or other matters as needed. See sections on Greek/Latin classics and electronic book formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing microform editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works consulted in microform editions should be cited according to the format of the original publication and additionally specify the microform format actually consulted (e.g., microfiche or microfilm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include locators appropriate to the microform (e.g., fiche and frame numbers and row letter). Examples: microfiche, p. 67, 3C12; microfilm for dissertations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume numbers and page numbers (numerals and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In source citations, volume numbers are always given in arabic numerals. If the volume number is immediately followed by a page number, the abbreviation vol. is omitted and a colon separates the volume number from the page number with no intervening space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See examples throughout section for formatting (e.g., 4:243).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing a multivolume work as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: When a multivolume work is cited as a whole, the total number of volumes is given after the title of the work (or after the editor’s name if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If volumes were published over several years, give dates of the first and last volumes separated by an en dash. See also 14.78.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing a particular volume in a note
rubrics_metrics.description: If a particular volume of a multivolume work is cited, give the volume number and the individual volume title if there is one, in addition to the general title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If volumes have been published in different years, give only the date of the cited volume. A short form may omit the individual volume title when logical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing a particular volume in a bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: If only one volume of a multivolume work is of interest, it may be listed alone in different valid ways (author/editor ordering variations are acceptable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If editor(s) differ for series and individual volume, include both where appropriate. Publication date should normally correspond to the last-mentioned title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters and parts of individual volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific parts of individual volumes of multivolume books are cited in the same way as parts of single-volume books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a note referring to the entire chapter, a chapter number, if available, may replace page numbers (e.g., 'vol. 3, chap. 9').

rubrics_metrics.name: One volume published as two or more physical books
rubrics_metrics.description: If a single volume of a multivolume work has been published as two or more physical books, the reference must include book as well as volume number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: vol. 2, bk. 3, The Scholarly Disciplines, with the book number stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors and editors of multivolume works (naming order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some multivolume works have both a general editor and individual editors or authors for each volume; when individual volumes are cited, the editor’s or translator’s name follows the part for which he or she is responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include additional editors for new editions as needed; examples show different acceptable orderings depending on emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series titles, numbers, and editors (inclusion and formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Including a series title in a citation helps readers decide whether to pursue a reference, but may be omitted if the book can be located without it; if included, the series title is capitalized headline-style but not italicized or in quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the series is numbered, the number follows the series title with no intervening comma unless 'vol.' or 'no.' is used. For non-English series titles use sentence style. Series editor name is usually omitted unless needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating a series as a multivolume work
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of series may lend themselves to being cited as a whole and in such cases the series may be treated as a multivolume work with the title of the series in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually it is preferable to cite individual titles and include the series title in roman; examples show both treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multivolume work within a series (numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a book within a series consists of more than one volume, the number of volumes or the volume number (if reference is to a particular volume) follows the book title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include series name and number formatting as appropriate; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old series and new series notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some numbered series restart numbering; notation such as n.s. (new series) or 2nd ser. may be used (usually enclosed in commas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books in the old series may be identified by o.s., 1st ser., or similar notations as complements to the new series notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts of publication (place, publisher, date format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditionally, facts of publication for books include place (city), publisher, and date (year). These elements are put in parentheses in a note but not in a bibliography; a colon appears between place and publisher, and the date follows the publisher preceded by a comma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Virginia Woolf, To the Lighthouse (London: Hogarth Press, 1927). See 14.23 for cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place and date only for pre-1900 books
rubrics_metrics.description: For books published before 1900 it is acceptable to omit publishers’ names and include only the place and date of publication; a comma, not a colon, follows the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formats: The Vicar of Wakefield (Salisbury, 1766).

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of publication—which city to include
rubrics_metrics.description: The place to be included is the city that usually appears on the title page (or copyright page) — the city where the publisher’s main editorial offices are located; if two or more cities are given, only the first is normally included in the citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples list common publishers and cities; follow what appears on the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to specify state/province/country
rubrics_metrics.description: If the city of publication may be unknown to readers or confused with another city of the same name, add the abbreviation of the state, province, or country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chicago prefers two-letter postal codes (IL, MA), though some publishers prefer conventional abbreviations. Washington is followed by DC; major cities such as Los Angeles and Baltimore need no state abbreviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: City names in languages other than English
rubrics_metrics.description: Current, commonly used English names for cities are usually preferred whenever such forms exist; if in doubt, record the name of the city as it appears with the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use 'Belgrade' (not Beograd), 'Munich' (not München), 'Mexico City' (not México). See 11.83 for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No place of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When the place of publication is not known, use n.p. (or N.p. if following a period) before the publisher’s name. If the place can be surmised, it may be given with a question mark in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (n.p.: Windsor, 1910) or ([Lake Bluff, IL?]: Vliet & Edwards, 1890). For many modern self-published works omit place if none is listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred form of publisher’s name
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher’s name may be given either in full or in somewhat abbreviated form; shorter forms are preferred in most bibliographies, but the form should reflect the publisher’s name at the date of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify publisher name as of publication via Library of Congress, WorldCat, Books in Print, etc. For reprints see 14.113-15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omissible parts of a publisher’s name
rubrics_metrics.description: In notes and bibliographies omit an initial 'The' and corporate suffixes such as Inc., Ltd., Co., S.A., etc.; 'Books' is usually retained; 'Press' should not be omitted from a university press name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain given names or initials preceding family names. Examples: 'Houghton Mifflin' not 'Houghton Mifflin Co.'; 'Little, Brown' not 'Little, Brown & Co.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'and' versus ampersand in publisher names
rubrics_metrics.description: Either 'and' or '&' may be used in a publisher’s name regardless of how it appears on the title page; choose one form and use it consistently throughout a bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the publisher’s name is not in English, use the equivalent of 'and' unless an ampersand is used on the title page. Serial comma conventions differ depending on 'and' vs '&' (see examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English publishers’ names (translation and abbreviations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not translate any part of a publisher’s name in a language other than English; omit corporate abbreviations corresponding to Inc. or Ltd. (e.g., German GmbH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization should follow the original unless the name appears in full capitals, in which case use headline-style capitalization. Examples given for Mexico City, Munich, Paris publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing self-published or privately published books
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite self-published books according to information on the title or copyright page; use language such as 'self-published' (abbreviated 'self-pub.' in a note but not in a bibliography) or 'printed by the author.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For works distributed via commercial self-publishing platforms, include the platform or distributor name; for e-books add the app/device or file format (e.g., iBooks, EPUB, Kindle). If place is not listed, it may be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent companies, imprints, and which name to cite
rubrics_metrics.description: When a parent company’s name appears in addition to the publisher’s imprint, it is usually sufficient to cite the imprint; if unclear which name to list, consult catalogs and, if still unclear, include both separated by a slash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: cite as 'Scribner Paperback Fiction' rather than Simon & Schuster unless context requires the parent name; if unsure, use 'Imprint / Parent Publisher'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special academic imprints and joint imprints
rubrics_metrics.description: If an academic publisher issues a book through a special division, imprint, or publishing consortium, specify the imprint arrangement when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show 'Belknap Press of Harvard University Press' and 'Northeastern University Press, an imprint of University Press of New England.' Provide state if needed for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copublication (when two publishers are listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: When books are published simultaneously by two publishers (often in different countries), usually only the publisher more relevant to the users of the citation need be listed; if both are listed, separate them with a semicolon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dates differ for the copublications, record both dates. For copublications between a publisher and an institution (e.g., a museum), handle similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed books (publisher vs distributor)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a book published by one company and distributed by another, use the name on the title page; the distributor’s name is usually omitted unless essential to users of a bibliography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If wording indicates 'Published by arrangement with...' that phrase may be included if of particular interest. For retail self-publishing distributors see section on self-published works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date—include only year
rubrics_metrics.description: For books include only the year (not month or day) as the publication date; the date is found on the title page or copyright page and usually corresponds to the copyright date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more copyright dates appear, the most recent indicates the publication date. For any edition other than the first, include the edition and the date of that edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing publication date from impressions or copyright renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not confuse the publication date with the date of a subsequent printing (impression) or a renewal of copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements like '53rd impression' or 'Copyright renewed 1980' should be disregarded when determining publication date; for new editions vs impressions see 1.26 and 14.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date ranges for multivolume works published over years
rubrics_metrics.description: When an entire multivolume, multiyear work is cited, give the range of dates for first to last volume; if the work has not been completed, give the date of the first volume followed by an en dash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single volume is cited, give only the date of that volume. See 6.78-79 for punctuation rules with the en dash.

rubrics_metrics.name: No date of publication (use of n.d.)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the publication date of a printed work cannot be ascertained, use the abbreviation n.d. in place of the year; a guessed-at date may be given in brackets or with 'ca.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Boston, n.d.; Edinburgh, [1750?] or Edinburgh, n.d., ca. 1750. Works with no publisher/place/date should be included in a bibliography only if accompanied by the location where a copy can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forthcoming publications (how to cite)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a book is under contract and already titled but the date is not yet known, use 'forthcoming' in place of the date; 'in press' is more specific but 'forthcoming' is recommended as more inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If page numbers are available they may be given. Use '(Place: Publisher, forthcoming)' format. Reprinted citations need not be updated; revised editions may be updated after checking quotations and pagination.
